rationale: Domain first: a ban is a verdict on a worker's own behaviour (spammy, fast, low-quality answers reflected in the 10 profile/performance statistics), not on who they sat next to. Edges here mean 'worked on the same task', which is task-driven co-participation rather than a trust or collusion tie, so the structure is dense and indiscriminate (avg_degree 88.3, density 0.0150, clustering 0.533) and every banned worker shares tasks with mostly legitimate ones. With homophily 0.749 the neighbourhoods are dominated by normal workers, so purely neighbour-agreement views (local_affinity, community) would rank boundary and bridging nodes, not cheats. That points to attribute-space views with a global notion of 'normal worker'. one_class leads: SVDD on the embedding places the bulk of compliant workers inside a boundary and pushes out profiles whose performance statistics sit outside it, which is exactly the banned-worker signature in a low-dimensional (feature_dim 10), non-power-law (is_power_law false) feature space where a single well-populated normal region genuinely exists. reconstruction is the complementary conditional view: an autoencoder learns each statistic as predicted from the co-task neighbourhood, so a worker whose numbers are inconsistent with the peers who handled the same tasks leaves a residual, which also absorbs the task-difficulty context that a purely global boundary ignores. attr_struct_mismatch supplies the third, genuinely orthogonal (cross-modal) view and is the best-separated landmarker on offer: p50 0.314 rising to p90 0.718 and p99 0.914, a long clean upper tail, and its mechanism matches the domain, a banned worker is structurally unremarkable (ordinary degree, sits in one of the 26 communities, modularity 0.519) while ranking abnormally on attributes, and that attribute-versus-structure divergence is precisely what camouflage inside shared task pools looks like. Deliberately excluded: density is degenerate (p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0, mean 0.0023), kNN distances collapse in 10 duplicated dimensions (feature_dup_rate 0.489) so it carries almost no ranking information; conformity is saturated rather than separated (mean 0.811, p50 0.870, p99 0.969, a compressed tail in which almost everyone is 'conformant'), and its duplication trigger is an artefact of low-dimensional discretised performance counters rather than evidence of template profiles, banned tolokers are deviant performers, not minimal-profile hiders; local_affinity, homophily_violation and spectral are all local-agreement restatements that would be largely redundant with the reconstruction residual while being more diluted by the shared-task edge semantics.

Banned tolokers are workers gaming a crowdsourcing platform: they spam-complete tasks for payout, so their profile/performance vector is not an exotic outlier but a minimal, template-like record (feature_dim = 10, feature_sparsity = 0.4803, feature_dup_rate = 0.489 - nearly half the rows are duplicates of a dominant pattern). That is the camouflage-by-conformity regime, and the landmarker confirms a dense conformant mass with structure in it (conformity mean 0.8111, p50 0.8696): the deviant-feature paradigms are looking for the wrong thing here, since a banned worker's stats sit inside the bulk. Conformity leads for that reason. attr_struct_mismatch is the complementary cross-modal view and has the sharpest tail of all landmarkers (p50 0.3138 -> p90 0.7175 -> p99 0.9141, std 0.2454): a worker whose profile reads normal but whose co-task footprint does not is exactly the ban signature, and it reads a different modality than conformity's purely feature-space residual. local_affinity adds the neighbourhood view that the domain supports - homophily = 0.7492 means co-task partners genuinely resemble each other, so a worker who disagrees with the people they share tasks with is informative, and its tail is separated (p50 0.1982 -> p99 0.6969). community completes the set on structure: edges are 'worked on the same task', clustering_coeff = 0.5329 and modularity = 0.5194 over 26 communities mean the projects form real task blocks, and abusive workers spread indiscriminately across projects rather than adhering to one block (p50 0.2295 -> p99 0.7341). Rejected: density is degenerate (p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0, no usable ranking) at avg_degree 88.28 where kNN in embedding space saturates; homophily_violation is near-redundant with local_affinity and would double-count the same neighbourhood view; reconstruction, contrastive, adversarial and one_class all rest on anomalies being hard to reconstruct or lying outside the normal boundary, which is the opposite of what feature_dup_rate = 0.489 plus the conformity distribution indicate; spectral is the weakest landmarker (p99 only 0.5512) and spectral_gap = 0.132 with no power-law degree structure gives little high-frequency purchase.

Domain first: banned tolokers are workers who game a crowdsourcing platform, and an edge here only means 'co-worked a task', which is a weak, extremely dense relation (avg_degree 88.3, density 0.0150, clustering 0.5329). Banned workers therefore do not sit in sparse or peripheral regions of the graph, they sit inside the busiest task pools, often alongside legitimate workers on the same tasks. That rules out the outlier-in-embedding-space family: density is a degenerate landmarker here (p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0, mean 0.0023), so kNN/LOF finds no low-density region at all, and one_class/adversarial rely on the same 'anomaly lies outside the normal boundary' premise that a 10-dimensional profile-statistics feature space with 48.9% duplicate rows cannot support. Reconstruction is also poorly matched: with feature_dim = 10 and feature_sparsity 0.4803, an autoencoder mostly re-learns the template, and the abusers are precisely the ones whose profile stats look ordinary. conformity is first because it inverts exactly that failure: feature_dup_rate = 0.489 means the feature matrix is template-dominated, and a banned worker's defence is to keep profile and performance statistics indistinguishable from the bulk (minimal effort, plausible accuracy, generic profile). Its distribution is the most mass-concentrated of all landmarkers (mean 0.8111, p50 0.8696), consistent with a large conformant core that the negative-residual direction can rank inside. attr_struct_mismatch is the strongest separated tail on offer (p50 0.3138 to p95 0.7991 to p99 0.9141, std 0.2454) and is the right cross-modal question for this task: a ban is a behavioural verdict, so the signal is a worker whose profile/performance attributes disagree with the company they keep in the task graph, e.g. ordinary-looking stats but an unusual co-working footprint, or heavy co-working with a degree profile the attributes do not justify (max_degree 2138 vs avg 88.3, degree_std 161.8). local_affinity adds the neighbour-level view that homophily = 0.7492 licenses: with well-behaved workers agreeing with their task partners, a worker who disagrees with the partners they share tasks with is the local, per-edge form of the same suspicion, and its tail is real if modest (p50 0.1982 to p99 0.6969). community is the complementary meso-scale view: modularity 0.5194 over 26 communities means the 13 projects induce genuine task-pool structure, and 'fits no project pool well' is a different failure mode from either the neighbour-level or cross-modal one, catching workers who spread thinly across pools rather than belonging to one (p50 0.2295 to p95 0.5989). I deliberately drop homophily_violation despite its healthy tail, because it asks nearly the same feature-neighbour-mismatch question as local_affinity and attr_struct_mismatch and would make the set redundant, and I drop spectral (weak, compressed tail: p50 0.1077, p95 0.4157, and spectral_gap 0.132 on a dense clustered graph makes high-frequency response mostly a degree artefact). The final set spans four genuinely different axes: feature-space in-lierness (conformity), cross-modal rank divergence (attr_struct_mismatch), neighbour-level disagreement (local_affinity), and meso-scale community adherence (community).
